metadata.name: updatedb
metadata.description: Update the filename database used by locate

installation.note: updatedb is typically installed with locate (plocate/mlocate). Many systems run it automatically via a daily timer/cron.

overview.summary: updatedb rebuilds or refreshes the database that locate searches. Running it makes locate results include newly created files and remove entries for deleted files (depending on configuration). It often requires elevated permissions to scan system directories.
when_to_use: locate results are missing a file you just created
locate is showing paths that no longer exist
You want locate searches to reflect recent filesystem changes

syntax.description: updatedb scans the filesystem based on its configuration and writes the locate database file.

options.description: Show help and available options (varies by implementation)
options.use_case: Check supported flags for your distro's implementation

examples.title: Refresh the locate database now
examples.description: Update the locate database so locate returns up-to-date results
examples.use_case: After creating/moving files you want to find with locate

common_pitfalls.description: Without sudo, updatedb may skip system directories and produce incomplete results.
common_pitfalls.solution: Run with sudo if you want a full-system database (sudo updatedb).

common_pitfalls.issue: It can take time on large disks
common_pitfalls.description: Database rebuilds scan many paths and can be slow on systems with lots of files.
common_pitfalls.solution: Let the scheduled job run, or run updatedb during low-usage periods.

related_commands.description: Searches the database produced by updatedb
